title: Can A.I. remove the edge for traders from the market ?
author: TradeWithNandi
selftext:
This thought has been going on in my mind since 2023, that as the AI models become smarter and say even cheaper, then it would become much easier to spot and execute trading opportunities (pair it with easy API integration with the broking platform).

Eventually that would create a level playing field for many causing the edge to become thinner with time, thus reducing trading opportunities even further.

Only strict regulations in predicitve models can somewhat prevent this, but I fear that it cannot be curbed beyong a point.

As far as the question of strategies being different is concerned, i agree that there is no end to human greed and fear, but what if the models can spot and execute with minimum input from the trader and it is accessible to everyone.

At times sounds good for many, but I believe that might lead to disappearance of many traders as their margins might reduce.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: It can thin out the simple edges, yes. Anything that's easy for everyone to spot gets crowded, and crowded signals tend to stop paying, which is true with or without AI. What tends to last longer is the part that's harder to copy, like good risk control and sizing, and the discipline to stop a strategy once it quits working. That means checking regularly whether an idea still holds on recent data. Cymetica's Backtest Labs holds out the last part of the history, which is a handy way to see if an edge has faded lately.

comments.author: boybitschua
comments.body: Can it? I had it try to build a novel strategy from various papers and it is unable to come up with something profitable. This is no different from the blogging era where a lot think just because you can create a blog it is easy money. All of the edges strategies out there are already gone/arbed out even before AI. So if we are expecting the common guy going to get something out of it, im not betting on it. The companies selling shovels will surely win.

replies.author: TradeWithNandi
replies.body: Naahh..I think people who know trading will get huge advantage using AI tools. Lol my imagination goes to the point where a semi-sentient tool analyses trade patterns and then takes over eventually manipulating the market (say for a big player) assuming the regulator has not put checks and balances in place (though I feel SEBI has done quite a good job in increasing compliance)
